1.why: All eight screens show a static, uncluttered layout with no animations, carousels, or pop-ups.

2.why: Bold headings, high-contrast teal buttons, and yellow warning boxes make primary actions and alerts visually dominant.

3.why: Each step has a single clear purpose and labeled field, though the persistent logs panel adds minor visual noise.

4.why: The flow requires six sequential steps plus memorizing complex password composition rules and copying long one-time tokens.

5.why: No password-manager, autofill, or remember-me controls appear on any screen.

6.why: The interface never surfaces previously saved credentials, contacts, or other familiar items for recognition.

7.why: Instructional sentences are brief and plainly worded on every step.

8.why: No error states or error messages are shown in any of the provided screenshots.

9.why: Simulated MFA and recovery codes are displayed as examples, yet no sample password format is illustrated.

10.why: The flow offers only a single password-recovery path; no alternative choices such as face or code login are presented.

11.why: Each screen contains at most two fields and one primary button, avoiding choice overload.

12.why: Step labels, log updates, and the final green confirmation banner explicitly state the result of every action.

13.why: Phishing warnings, password-rule tips, and short step descriptions supply contextual help throughout.

14.why: Fields can be re-entered, but no explicit retry or back controls are visible and repeated failures are rate-limited.

15.why: Header, card layout, button style, and log panel remain identical across all eight steps.
